title: skin_map
description: The `skin_map` content kind (megaplan 1.7, 1.12, tasks 5-A2 and 5-F1): which skin and player model a Night City NPC figure wears, plus the two cyber skins of linked players. One row per file. An NPC matches a row when every match key the row has holds for the NPC's tags from the `npcs` message: `role` (the vendor type name of 2.31 `gamedataVendorType`, e.g. RipperDoc, Clothes, Drinks, or a content role: fixer, bartender, medic, mechanic, cyberpsycho), `faction` (Affiliation().EnumName(), 2.31 `gamedataAffiliation`, e.g. TygerClaws, NCPD), `gender` (male or female: `g` 1 or 2; an NPC whose `g` is 0 matches no row with `gender`) and `archetype` (`gamedataArchetypeType`, e.g. HeavyRangedT2). A key's value is one name or a list of names (any of them). Of the matching rows the highest `priority` (default 0) wins, then the row with more match keys, then, among rows still tied, one chosen by the NPC id (stable per NPC, so a crowd mixes the tied skins). A row with no match keys matches every NPC (the shipped `default` row). Rows with `cyber` are the skins of linked players (male: classic, female: slim) and never match an NPC. `texture` is the full resource id of a 64x64 skin PNG (`<namespace>:textures/entity/...png`, shipped in the mod or added by a resource pack); `model` is the player model to draw it on: `classic` (4 px arms) or `slim` (3 px arms). A row without `gender` should use the classic model (unknown gender is drawn classic). A file with the same id as a default replaces it, so a datapack can restyle one faction or add a row with a higher priority.
